"Already froze the branch before I sent the ping, sweetheart, your live push isn't going anywhere."

"You did what? Kitty, if you sandboxed a mid-compile thread, you just buried the third fault under forty layers of garbage logs!"

All three monitors flashed stark white, dumped a rolling wall of FAILED ROLLBACK lines, and triggered a sharp containment chime from the ceiling vent. His right-eye interface threw a violent smear of ghosted hexadecimal across the dark lens of his brow.

"Session is over, Gabrielle." Zephyr said. Watching the flushed scorch stripe above his brow, Zephyr felt a cold, steady tightness settle behind his ribs.

"You had forty hours without anyone hovering. You lost an eyebrow and blew a live conduit."

The heavy bulkhead groaned shut behind them, shearing the roar of the cooling fans down to a distant vibration beneath the deck plates.

Ten feet ahead, the lift doors chimed without being called, slid halfway apart with a grinding shudder, and jammed hard against a glitching proximity sensor. The overhead strips snapped violently into stark emergency crimson.

"Looks like Kitty's sandbox is leaking, big guy. Still want to lock me in a dark room while the hallway eats itself?"
